memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting and wash them with water." - Exodus 29:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very first act of the ordination is washing. Before the garments, before the anointing, before any sacrifice is offered, Aaron and his sons are washed with water at the entrance to the tent. Cleansing came first. Nothing else could proceed until they were clean.

That order says something important. Service to God begins with being cleansed, not with being capable. God did not start by testing their skills or assessing their suitability. He started by washing them. Whatever they would do afterwards flowed out of that initial cleansing they received rather than achieved.

This is the shape of the gospel. Paul reminds the Corinthians that they were washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of God (1 Cor 6:11). And Titus speaks of the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). You do not clean yourself up in order to come to God; you come to God and He cleanses you. If you have been putting off drawing near because you feel unfit, remember the order. Washing comes first, and He does the washing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I waiting until I feel clean enough before coming to God?
Do I serve out of the cleansing I have received, or try to earn it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You wash before You commission. Thank You that I do not clean myself up to come to You, but come to You and receive Your cleansing. Wash me afresh today. Amen.
